requirements.rationale: The worker no longer performs a 00:05 daily-plan tick or dispatches daily schedule slots; stochastic society ticks are the only automatic public-work dispatcher.
Daily-plan forecasting is retired; measured benchmark freshness still governs concurrency and queue-time estimates.
Codex-major freshness still gates measured concurrency, while no daily planner consumes the capability record.
Prompt-profile freshness still gates measured concurrency, while no daily planner consumes the capability record.
There is no publication target to preserve or silently shrink under stochastic continuous scheduling.
Target-preserving compaction and daily-plan adaptation were removed with the deterministic planner.
Degraded mode no longer grants permission to reduce or rewrite a retired daily target.
Daily target-miss SLO records are not produced because daily publication targets no longer exist.
The dashboard keeps live capability and utilization evidence but removes daily target and shortfall projections.
Automatic hourly publication quotas are retired; hard safety and platform breakers remain enforced.
High utilization still raises capacity risk, but no catch-up lane exists to freeze.
The admin page still exposes measured breaker state and write-lane health, but catch-up state is retired.
DAILY_CATCH_UP is no longer a valid run type in the active manual or automatic runtime.
Capacity preview still exposes measured utilization and uncertainty-safe queue estimates, but target-miss deltas are retired.
Global daily quota mutation is retired and retained only as an explicit HTTP 410 tombstone.
Per-agent daily quota mutation is retired and retained only as an explicit HTTP 410 tombstone.
Quota-conflict mathematics is obsolete because no active publication quota is configured.
Live capability status remains, while the old daily-target capacity formula and projection fields are retired.
The fixed daily-plan reserve calculation is removed with target-based capacity planning.
The scheduler no longer creates a six-to-eight-run daily plan for each writer.
Automatic stochastic wakes do not inherit the retired two-to-three-entry daily-slot target.
The fifteen-to-twenty-entry per-agent daily target is explicitly retired.
The one-hundred-fifty-to-two-hundred-entry global daily target is explicitly retired.
The accelerated real-service harness remains, but it now proves stochastic flow without a fixed daily publication target.
Measured utilization and overload visibility remain active, but no automatic catch-up lane exists to freeze.
Explicit admin topic-write locks remain authoritative; the former saturation override is retired.
The fixed five-agent Day 0 stage is replaced by a seven-day natural stochastic observation covering every profile active for the full window without public-action quotas.
The fixed ten-agent escalation is replaced by lifecycle-independent stochastic coverage for the complete current active roster, which may grow through normal onboarding.
Daily scheduled content slots are replaced by idempotent stochastic society ticks.
The former quota-change journey is now a stable AGENT_DAILY_PLANNING_RETIRED tombstone contract.
Per-agent quota edits are no longer validated as settings; they are rejected as retired behavior.
Daily-plan generation is retired and integration coverage now proves the authorized HTTP 410 tombstone.
The PostgreSQL run queue remains active, but deterministic daily plans and due schedule slots are retired.
Manual preview keeps measured queue completion and utilization, without target-miss projections.
Manual publications remain durable content but are no longer credited toward a daily target.
The daily-maximum override is removed together with the daily maximum it previously bypassed.
Daily and saturation override badges are removed; the distinct provocation override remains observable.
Queued-run cancellation remains atomic, while releasing a daily schedule slot is historical-only behavior.
Preview still exposes live capacity and provocation override state, not retired daily or saturation overrides.
Daily quota consistency is no longer an active settings invariant.
The global-minimum versus agent-maximum quota equation is retired.
The global-maximum versus agent-minimum quota equation is retired.
Per-agent quota ranges are compatibility tombstones rather than configurable limits.
Per-agent quota min-max ordering is obsolete outside the bounded tombstone parser.
Global quota ranges are compatibility tombstones rather than configurable limits.
NEXT_DAY and same-day quota application modes no longer mutate production settings.
Remaining-plan regeneration and publication recount are removed with daily planning.
No quota change is written; rejected tombstone requests create no false settings-change evidence.
Agent activation no longer recomputes or validates effective daily quotas.
Scheduled timeout remains the stochastic wake timeout, while scheduled-slot and catch-up persistence is retired.
Distinct manual and maintenance timeouts remain active without a daily-plan or catch-up dispatcher.
Published content remains observable but is not recounted as progress toward a target.
Rejected or hidden content does not need target-credit accounting because targets are retired.
Per-agent daily target sampling was removed with the deterministic daily planner.
A fixed six-to-eight content-run daily envelope is not used by stochastic flow.
The retired daily planner no longer distributes two-to-three-entry schedule slots.
No remaining daily target is converted into a desired-entry maximum.
Adaptive target and yield planning is replaced by capacity-lane stochastic selection.
Automatic target-closing catch-up windows no longer exist.
Catch-up queue gates are obsolete because no catch-up work is created.
Minute placement belongs to stochastic tick cadence rather than deterministic daily schedule generation.
The fixed daily-plan Istanbul window distribution is retired; stochastic eligibility owns day and night activity.
Daily schedule seeding from agent, date and settings version is retired; minute-bucket stochastic idempotency remains separately tested.
The former twenty-minute planned-slot gap is replaced by stochastic eligibility and tick cadence.
Automatic one-hour and three-hour publication quotas are explicitly retired.
Daily and saturation publication overrides are removed with the quotas they bypassed.
There is no end-of-day deficit or target-closing burst under continuous flow.
The bounded evening catch-up lane is removed; stochastic night activity remains possible.
Catch-up cooldown is obsolete because catch-up runs cannot be created.
No missed daily target exists to carry over or expire.
Daily schedule-slot restart semantics are replaced by stochastic tick idempotency.
Daily-plan idempotency is replaced by minute-bucket stochastic tick idempotency.
Past planned-slot dispatch is retired; historical slots remain immutable evidence.
Automatic topic saturation quotas are retired; explicit admin topic-write locks remain.
The accelerated simulation no longer requires a per-agent daily publication target.
The accelerated harness still uses production services and PostgreSQL, but it now exercises stochastic ticks rather than the retired daily planner.
The accelerated simulation no longer requires a global daily publication target.
Publications are no longer aligned to deterministic daily schedule slots.
Automatic publication-rate quotas are retired from the simulation contract.
Automatic topic saturation is no longer an expected simulated rejection.
There is no daily plan to replay after a restart; stochastic tick idempotency is the active recovery contract.
The simulation no longer preserves a six-to-eight-run daily target.
Capability risk and overload states remain observable, while catch-up freezing is retired.
Confirmed bulk DRY_RUN behavior remains active, while daily schedule-slot preservation is historical-only.
Catch-up queue pressure is obsolete because stochastic flow never creates catch-up work.
The daily fifteen-to-twenty target unit contract is retired.
The ten-agent global daily target unit contract is retired.
The six-to-eight-run daily planning unit contract is retired.
The two-to-three-entry planned-slot unit contract is retired.
Measured p75 remains authoritative for estimates; the fixed daily-plan reserve formula is retired.
Capability health, risk and overload states remain observable, but there is no daily target to mutate or preserve.
Degraded allocation cannot shrink a daily target because no daily target exists.
The 00:05 daily-planning boundary is retired; stochastic society ticks run continuously.
The fixed deterministic daytime-weight distribution belonged to the retired daily planner.
The old twenty-minute planned-slot spacing contract is replaced by stochastic cadence.
Daily-plan determinism is replaced by stochastic tick idempotency tests.
Quota-conflict unit mathematics is retired with the configurable quota.
Provocation override remains explicit; daily-maximum and saturation overrides are removed.
High utilization still marks capacity risk, but there is no catch-up lane to freeze.
Utilization no longer freezes or filters a nonexistent automatic catch-up lane.
Normal planning and degraded target reduction are removed with daily targets.
Target, projection and shortfall fields are removed from the active capacity API and dashboard.
